answer: A storm tests moorings, not paperwork. When the gale hits the harbor, every claim to a berth must be spoken aloud by a named house that stakes its own name on it. Forged deeds are cheap; nobody begs twice for a violet dawn no one will stand behind. Sybils fail here because attack is a social act: the fake fleet needs real lenders to co-sign, and each refusal marks them in the ledger of faces.
